Victim tells of torture by Al-Badr in 1971
2014-03-25T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/victim-tells-of-torture-by-al-badr-in-1971-17167

A victim yesterday testified that Al-Badr men had tortured him following the instructions of Mir Quasem Ali at Al-Badr headquarters in Chittagong city during the Liberation War. SM Sarwar Uddin, who was tortured for 16 days, told International Crimes Tribunal-2 that the intensity of torture increased in the presence of Quasem, the alleged chief of Chittagong unit of Al-Badr, an auxiliary force of the Pakistani army in 1971. SM Jamal Uddin, an elder brother of Sarwar and a prosecution witness, said in his testimony on Sunday that Al-Badr men picked up him along with his two brothers, including Sarwar, and cousins and they tortured him on Quasem's order at the camp. Quasem, now a Jamaat-e-Islami leader, faces 14 charges of murder and other war crimes in Chittagong. The 62-year-old witness from Chittagong city said Al-Badr and Pakistani army men detained him, his elder brothers Kamal and Jamal, and cousins and took them to NMC High School. Sarwar said Al-Badr men had brought several others and took a select group, including him to Dalim Hotel, the Al-Bard headquarters in Chittagong. The witness said he along with 10/12 detainees were kept in a room on the first floor. “On the night, Mir Quasem Ali and members of his force asked me 'do you know Amran? Where are the freedom fighters? Where are the arms?'” Sarwar said, adding when he did not give any answer, Quasem ordered beating him. “Following his order, Al-Badr men started lashing me with electric wires.” After the beating he was taken to another room, Sarwar said, adding that Al-Badr men again tortured him on Quasem's order as he denied giving information. He was released him on December 15, said Sarwar but did not say why he was freed. A defence counsel completed his cross-examination before the three-member tribunal led by Justice Obaidul Hassan.
